raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

**Depends on #54061.** This branch is #54061 plus one commit, `[Profiler] Record the graph warm-up next to its capture`; only that commit is new here. I will rebase it when #54061 changes. @devalshahamd, happy to fold this into #54061 instead if you prefer.

With `capture_torch_profiler` on, #54061 writes one trace per captured shape, holding the capture under `capture_<tokens>_<mode>`. This also records the eager warm-up that runs just before the capture, in the same trace, under `warmup_<tokens>_<mode>`.

Why: a graph capture records its launches without running them, so the capture trace carries no kernel names, and a replayed graph can run on several streams. The warm-up runs the same forward eagerly for the same batch descriptor, so its kernels name, in order, the launches the capture records. That is what lets a replayed decode step be attributed to the code that issued each kernel.

How:
- `graph_capture_shape()` holds one profiler session open across a shape's warm-up and capture; `graph_capture_warmup()` and `graph_capture_step()` record into it.
- Outside `graph_capture_shape()`, `graph_capture_step()` opens its own session as before, so the encoder and speculator capture loops are unchanged.
- Applied to the V2 `CudaGraphManager.capture` and the V1 runner's `_warmup_and_capture`.

The warm-up only adds to the trace when `capture_torch_profiler` is on; nothing changes otherwise. The diff of `cudagraph_utils.py` and `gpu_model_runner.py` is mostly re-indentation (view with whitespace hidden).

## Before / after

The capture trace of the 16-token FULL decode graph of GLM-5.3-Flash on B200, opened in Perfetto. The "before" trace comes from a TP4 run with capture recording only, the "after" from a TP8 run with this change; the graph shape is the same.

**Before (capture only).** During capture the GPU does not run the captured kernels, it only records them. So the CPU side of the trace has every launch call, with its Python stack, but no launch reaches a kernel: of the ~1,400 kernel launch calls made while the forward is captured (746 `cuLaunchKernelEx`, 356 `cudaLaunchKernelExC`, 309 `cudaLaunchKernel`), none has a GPU kernel at the other end, so none has a kernel name or stream. Below, one of them selected: `Glm5NextDecoderLayer_3` → `Glm5NextMLAAttention_0` → `Indexer_0` → `aten::linear` → `aten::mm` → `cuLaunchKernelEx`. The stack says exactly which module launched it, but the launch has only a correlation id and no flow to a kernel (the after shot below shows that flow), so nothing says which kernel it was.

![before: a captured launch with no kernel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amd-sriram/vllm/e1b73bb3cfac0b5a201d57f414a04d930d44414b/pr2_before_captured_launch.png)

The only GPU events in the `capture_16_FULL` span are input and metadata preparation that runs eagerly around the forward. Area-selecting the span lists all of them: 12 device-to-device copies and 44 small kernels (fills, `arange`, `indexSelectSmallIndex`, `searchsorted`, `_indexer_decode_metadata_kernel`, `sm100_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`, ...), about 0.1 ms in total. None of them is a GEMM, attention or MoE kernel.

![before: every GPU event in the capture span](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amd-sriram/vllm/df76765c413d048dcdd2138307658b3ea8f0f5bc/pr2_before_capture_kernels.png)

**After (warm-up + capture in the same trace).** The same launch, in the warm-up recorded just before the capture: same module stack (`Glm5NextDecoderLayer_3` → `Glm5NextMLAAttention_0` → `Indexer_0` → `aten::linear` → `aten::mm` → `cuLaunchKernelEx`), but now it has a following flow to the kernel it ran, `nvjet_sm100_tst_32x64_64x16_4x1_v_bz_splitK_TNN` on stream 95. Across the whole `warmup_16_FULL` span that holds for 1,391 kernels on 13 streams, in launch order, right before `capture_16_FULL`.

![after: the same launch, now with its kernel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amd-sriram/vllm/45a09ed509108d0171c4ebdbfac0e5e1e8da12b0/pr2_after_warmup_launch.png)

One warm-up kernel selected: its name, its stream and the flow back to the CPU launch that issued it.

![after, one kernel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/amd-sriram/vllm/59fc23655c34b382a784f65c0af00d2d0765439c/pr2_after_warmup_kernel.png)

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_profiler.py
```

New tests: warm-up and capture share one session per shape, in that order; the warm-up label follows the binding's prefix; the shape session closes when the capture raises; `CudaGraphManager.capture` and the V1 `_warmup_and_capture` record the warm-up before the capture in one session.

## Test Result

The new tests pass. The same recording, carried in our serving images, names every kernel in the captured decode graphs of GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 on MI355X and B200, which we match against the replayed steps.

+    """CudaGraphManager.capture profiles each shape's warm-up and capture into

+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu import cudagraph_utils
+
+    manager = MagicMock()
+    manager.ubatch_runner = None
+    manager.use_breakable_cg = False

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Torch profiler helpers for CUDA/HIP graph capture tracing.
+
+Graph capture is driven by three subsystems (encoder, decoder and speculator)
+that reach the same handful of capture loops by different routes.
+``graph_capture_profiler`` binds one profiler around a subsystem's capture,
+and ``graph_capture_step`` picks that binding up inside whichever capture loop
+ends up running. Capture loops therefore carry no profiler plumbing, and a new
+speculator built on an existing capture loop is traced without further changes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextvars
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+from contextlib import AbstractContextManager, contextmanager
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_world_group
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.profiler.wrapper import (
+    TorchProfilerWrapper,
+    create_worker_profiler,
+    graph_capture_profiler_config,
+)
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class _CaptureBinding:
+    profiler: AbstractContextManager[Any]
+    label_prefix: str | None
+    # Every rank holds the same value: capture profiling is on and there are
+    # peers to keep in step with (see graph_capture_shape).
+    sync_ranks: bool = False
+
+
+_active_binding: contextvars.ContextVar[_CaptureBinding | None] = (
+    contextvars.ContextVar("vllm_graph_capture_binding", default=None)
+)
+_skip_capture_tracing: contextvars.ContextVar[bool] = contextvars.ContextVar(
+    "vllm_skip_graph_capture_tracing", default=False
+)
+_shape_open: contextvars.ContextVar[bool] = contextvars.ContextVar(
+    "vllm_graph_capture_shape_open", default=False
+)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def skip_graph_capture_tracing() -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Disable capture tracing for the throwaway memory-estimate capture."""
+    token = _skip_capture_tracing.set(True)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        _skip_capture_tracing.reset(token)
+
+
+def make_graph_capture_profiler(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    subsystem: str | None = None,
+) -> torch.profiler.profile | None:
+    """Build the one-shot capture profiler, or ``None`` when disabled."""
+    profiler_config = vllm_config.profiler_config
+    local_rank = get_world_group().local_rank
+    if local_rank != 0 or not profiler_config.capture_torch_profiler:
+        logger.info_once(
+            "Rank %d: Torch profiler disabled for GPU graph capture", local_rank
+        )
+        return None
+
+    capture_config = graph_capture_profiler_config(profiler_config)
+    worker_name = f"graph_capture_rank_{local_rank}"
+    if subsystem:
+        worker_name += f"_{subsystem}"
+    wrapper = create_worker_profiler(
+        capture_config, worker_name=worker_name, local_rank=local_rank
+    )
+    assert isinstance(wrapper, TorchProfilerWrapper)
+    # Serving creates wrapper.profiler only when a session starts. Capture
+    # needs the same settings without starting that session.
+    return wrapper.build_profiler()
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def graph_capture_profiler(
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+    subsystem: str | None = None,
+    label_prefix: str | None = None,
+) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Bind a graph-capture profiler for one subsystem's capture.
+
+    Args:
+        vllm_config: Engine config; used for profiler settings and device type.
+        subsystem: Suffix for the trace file name. ``"encoder"`` writes
+            ``graph_capture_rank_0_encoder.<timestamp>.pt.trace.json.gz``;
+            the main decoder passes ``None`` and keeps the unsuffixed name.
+        label_prefix: Inserted into every annotation recorded inside the
+            block, so that e.g. speculator graphs are labelled
+            ``capture_32_draft_FULL`` rather than reusing the decoder's
+            ``capture_32_FULL``.
+
+    """
+    if _skip_capture_tracing.get() or _active_binding.get() is not None:
+        yield
+        return
+
+    profiler = make_graph_capture_profiler(vllm_config, subsystem)
+    if profiler is None:
+        yield
+        return
+
+    binding = _CaptureBinding(
+        profiler=profiler,
+        label_prefix=label_prefix,
+        sync_ranks=bool(vllm_config.profiler_config.capture_torch_profiler)
+        and get_world_group().world_size > 1,
+    )
+    token = _active_binding.set(binding)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        _active_binding.reset(token)
+
+
+def _label(kind: str, num_tokens: int, mode: str, binding: _CaptureBinding) -> str:
+    if binding.label_prefix:
+        return f"{kind}_{num_tokens}_{binding.label_prefix}_{mode}"
+    return f"{kind}_{num_tokens}_{mode}"
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _profiled(binding: _CaptureBinding) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Enter the binding's profiler, unless a shape session already holds it."""
+    if _shape_open.get():
+        yield
+        return
+    token = _shape_open.set(True)
+    try:
+        with binding.profiler:
+            yield
+    finally:
+        _shape_open.reset(token)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def graph_capture_shape() -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Hold one profiler session open across a graph shape's warm-up and capture.
+
+    Without it each ``graph_capture_step`` opens its own session. Inside it,
+    ``graph_capture_warmup`` and ``graph_capture_step`` record into the same
+    session, so a shape's warm-up and capture land in one trace file. Does
+    nothing outside a ``graph_capture_profiler`` block.
+
+    With capture profiling on, every rank also waits for the others before the
+    shape starts. Only rank 0 records the capture, and saving each shape's trace
+    makes it slower than its peers, which otherwise run ahead: over a full
+    capture rank 0 falls minutes behind. A kernel whose ranks wait for each
+    other inside the launch, with a bound, then expires during the warm-up.
+    """
+    binding = _active_binding.get()
+    if binding is None:
+        yield
+        return
+    if binding.sync_ranks and not _shape_open.get():
+        get_world_group().barrier()
+    with _profiled(binding):
+        yield
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def graph_capture_warmup(num_tokens: int, mode: str) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Profile the eager warm-up that precedes a graph shape's capture.
+
+    Records a ``warmup_{num_tokens}_{mode}`` annotation (with the binding's
+    prefix, as ``graph_capture_step`` does). A captured graph records its
+    launches without running them, so the capture alone carries no kernel
+    names; the warm-up runs the same forward eagerly for the same batch
+    descriptor, so its kernels name the launches the capture records. Use it
+    inside ``graph_capture_shape`` so both land in the same trace. Does nothing
+    outside a ``graph_capture_profiler`` block.
+    """
+    binding = _active_binding.get()
+    if binding is None:
+        yield
+        return
+    with (
+        _profiled(binding),
+        torch.profiler.record_function(_label("warmup", num_tokens, mode, binding)),
+    ):
+        yield
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def graph_capture_step(num_tokens: int, mode: str) -> Iterator[None]:
+    """Profile the capture of a single graph shape.
+
+    Records a ``capture_{num_tokens}_{mode}`` annotation, or
+    ``capture_{num_tokens}_{label_prefix}_{mode}`` when the active binding
+    sets a prefix. Does nothing unless a ``graph_capture_profiler`` block is
+    actively profiling, so capture loops can call this unconditionally. Inside
+    ``graph_capture_shape`` it records into that shape's session instead of
+    opening its own.
+    """
+    binding = _active_binding.get()
+    if binding is None:
+        yield
+        return
+
+    with (
+        _profiled(binding),
+        torch.profiler.record_function(_label("capture", num_tokens, mode, binding)),
+    ):
+        yield
